brief: brief-js173.md and its follow-up: JS-173's fix has Refusal read its live-job check and its count of cores in one read-only snapshot, and has a worker's write that ends a job mark that worker seen (seen_at) in the same statement, whatever its liveness lock, so invariant 25's sentence 'Only a locked worker claims, forgets others and refreshes seen_at; a relocking one only reads its own row' is no longer literally true. Follow-up, by the lead's reading: the write is an UPDATE of the worker's row and never inserts; the liveness reaper does not read seen_at; but every reader other than Refusal counts a worker by seen_at alone within 10 s (alive and deliverability of a picked audio track or burnt-in subtitle, store agreement, the reason after a queue timeout, the room that a worker's placement, helpers and helper preemption see), and did before JS-173. Option B (refresh only with the lock held) built in a scratch copy: both sightings' checks pass 3 of 3, so the stopped-and-continued worker holds its lock, but TestAViewerWhoseJobCostsTwoGivenUpJobsTogetherIsNotRefused fails 3 of 3 on its precondition, undiagnosed, and passes 3 of 3 on the JS-173 build. Options: A2 reword and name the readers; A3 the same plus a follow-up making those readers lock-aware; B; C hold JS-173 until the readers are lock-aware.
tradeoff: Whether a fix that ends a wrong 'cannot be played' merges now with a stated, unmeasured widening (readers that count a worker by seen_at alone count a relocking worker for up to 10 s after it ends a job, as they already do after it loses its lock), or waits for a change to worker liveness or to those readers.
decision: accept (option A3: the sentence is reworded with the exception and the readers named; the readers' lock-awareness goes to the backlog)
serves: PRODUCT.md goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer. Starting, seeking, resuming, and recovering from a failure just work, for every film.' 'Failures are invisible.' 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'. DOMAINS.md invariant 25: 'Losing the liveness lock is not yet losing the lease'.
entry: Invariant 25's sentence is reworded: only a locked worker claims and forgets others, and only a locked worker's look refreshes seen_at; the one exception is the write by which a worker ends one of its own jobs, which marks that worker seen whatever its lock, changes its row only if it is still there, and never restores a forgotten worker's row; PlaybackInfo's refusal for cores still does not count a relocking worker; the readers that count a worker by seen_at alone are named, with what they may now do for up to `counted` after a relocking worker ends a job. JS-173 merges with that text. Given up: a viewer whose request (a picked audio track, a burnt-in subtitle, a job left for that worker, a helper not preempted) falls in that window on a worker that never retakes its lock may wait up to the queue timeout (6 s) or the rescue before being answered; before JS-173 the same held only for the 10 s after a lock loss. The fix changes when a worker is marked seen, not what a lease guarantees. Rejected: B (one of JS-173's checks fails 3 of 3 on it for an undiagnosed reason, and it is a fix round in worker liveness to protect readers that were never lock-aware); C (holds a fix for a wrong refusal forced 3 of 3, for a window no one has seen); A2 alone (the readers' gap would be stated and then forgotten). The first condition of this decision's earlier form held (the write never inserts); the second failed by the lead's reading and is answered here. A new backlog item holds making those readers count a worker only with its lock held. Triage with it: the record gains one line saying the first sighting's literal order passes on the unfixed tree and which stricter order forces it; which give-up paths the forced checks show (criterion 4) is asked of the lead, and any path not shown becomes a task beside JS-161 that does not hold this merge. Unverified when decided: how often a worker relocks for more than 10 s and ends a job meanwhile (none seen); the viewer's wait in the worst case (derived, not measured); why B changes the order in the two-jobs check, and whether that says anything about the build that merges (it passes there 3 of 3). Data that reopens it: the dogfood's logs showing a worker relocking for longer than `counted`; a queue timeout or late start within `counted` of a worker losing its lock; a job admitted for cores to a worker that does not hold its lock; JS-161 or JS-164 making one of the named readers decide an admission or a gauge, which promotes the backlog item into that task's design review.
